scopeReview: PSO-6.A.3–4: megacity/metacity scale and spatial patterns; suburbanization, decentralization, edge-city functions, exurbs, boomburbs and sprawl. Distinguishes size from global influence, core share from absolute change, and forms from measured consequences.
varietyReview: Four meaningful stimuli:consistent agglomeration counts, original peripheral-function map, metro redistribution chart and separated-versus-compact polygons. Checks classify thresholds, verify supplied functions/locations, compute shares and test nonoverlapping development geometry. Source/scale applications avoid universal city stereotypes.
repetitionReview: Different concepts and representations than6.1:population size categories, functional peripheral nodes, within-metropolitan redistribution and fragmentation. Definitions/boundaries explicit, no real-city ranking or numerical-only clone; varied keys and detailed options. Difficulty uncalibrated.
referenceNote: Primary institutional urban definitions and original boomburb research checked. All city populations, diagrams and field records synthetic; no copied question/map, exact contested threshold case or new resource. No independent human-review claim.

questions.independentReview: Checked8.5<10<12<20<22 with comparable agglomeration boundaries. Definitions explicitly supplied; no item depends on exactly20 million or a disputed current real-city estimate. UN/UN-Habitat primary descriptions corroborate approximate thresholds.

Verified mapped Core20,25, X60,20 and E85,48; field notes, not distance alone, supply job/retail and residential functions. No claim of satisfying every exact Garreau floor-area threshold or a universal Census exurb definition. Mobile inspection routed the illustrative corridor explicitly through X and placed its label farther left to avoid the X marker. Settlement positions and classifications are unchanged.

questions.correctOption: Outer municipalities gain residents faster, reducing the center’s share even while its population grows.
questions.independentReview: Independently computed totals2.0→3.1 million and center shares50%→35.48%; outer growth100%, center10%. Fixed metro components and classifications stated. Distinct from national urban/rural shares: this is within-metro redistribution. Mobile rendering exposed a floating-point axis tick at max2.4; the new chart now uses max4 and whole-number ticks without changing any values, labels, answers or ratios. All chart text is checked for long decimal artifacts.

questions.correctOption: New developed patches are spatially separated by intervening undeveloped land.
questions.independentReview: Checked separated X/Y/Z polygons with nonzero gaps and a single contiguous C polygon. Schematic polygon areas600 versus1200 illustrate contrasting footprints but no real hectares or commuter distances are inferred.

questions.correctOption: A boomburb: a large, rapidly growing suburban municipality.
questions.independentReview: Verified original Brookings book description:large rapidly growing incorporated communities over100000, not the region’s biggest city. No arbitrary exact annual-growth cutoff or current real city label imposed.

questions.correctOption: Major offices and shopping facilities shift to a peripheral employment center.
questions.independentReview: Separated functional decentralization from residence counts and ordinary natural increase. No assumption all suburbs contain jobs or all central businesses leave.

questions.correctOption: Exurban, with metropolitan ties despite a partly rural landscape.
questions.independentReview: Checked Census primary discussion acknowledges no single Bureau exurb definition and describes far-outer mixed rural/urban character. No universal legal boundary or density threshold asserted.

questions.correctOption: Municipal cores, continuous built-up areas and wider metropolitan regions may include different populations.
questions.independentReview: UN-Habitat urban-definition harmonization theme verified. No current city ranking or historical growth inferred from mismatched estimates.

questions.correctOption: The pattern describes a broad distributional tendency, while city sizes, histories and challenges still vary within and across regions.
questions.independentReview: Aligned PSO-6.A.3 without assigning actual countries a permanent income/world-system category or inventing a contemporary ranking. Broad tendency explicitly distinguished from universal classification.

questions.correctOption: Actual trip patterns, transport options, service-network lengths and costs, alongside population and land-use data.
questions.independentReview: Distinguished form from measured outcomes, avoiding a universal per-capita emissions or infrastructure-cost estimate. No real transport policy prescribed.

questions.correctOption: All suburbs are permanently identical bedroom communities with the same residents and jobs.
questions.independentReview: No real demographic group or city stereotyped. Conceptual distinction between dynamic urban forms and rigid labels, within6.2 scope rather than a new unsupported typology.
